questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose UZH as the academic opportunities for economics students are very broad. I got introduced to academic research on a very high level. In addition I chose Zürich because of the surrounding nature. I love to spend my weekends travelling or hiking in the mountains.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The only minus in the hygiene in my student house, and the covid restrictions in the beginning. Otherwise its been amazing!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The university provided me with any information I needed, and they are very good at remembering you about deadlines etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: My ESN buddy picked me up in the airport and we travelled together to my student house. After this I primarily used the student service at UZH for help. They are super nice and helpful. The easiest way to contract them is to go to their office at the university site.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: UZH also offered several welcome events with information about life in Switzerland, city tours, speed-friending etc. which was very helpful in the beginning.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Super easy. I got asked from UZH whether I want to apply for housing through them, which I said yes to. A month after I got the offer and signed a contract. It was very helpful that the university provided help, because the housing market in Zürich is crazy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You cannot live on-campus in Zürich, so everyone lives around the city. I lived at Meierweisenstrasse near Altstetten. It is a big student house with around 170 people. One of the good things of this is that you get to know a lot of people very easily as everyone is exchange students, and several parties/movie nights/dining nights are arranged in the house. It is also super cheap (for Zürich) as a room is around 550 chf per month. The disadvantageous is that everyone share one large kitchen, meaning that the hygiene standard is very low. I got sick several times in the beginning, but overall I think it was worth it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you get an offer from Meierweisenstrasse and you like to be social, then go for it :)

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university provided all the information I needed.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to register within the registration period. The only thing that was challenging was that the information sheet about course registration provided by the university was in German (hello google translate).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The university provided all the information I needed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty successful. I only had a seminar that I didn't get into. Otherwise I got all the courses I wanted. In general I think that most people get the courses they sign up for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: In the first two weeks you can try several courses and then drop those who you don't like, as the registration is open in these weeks. I used this opportunity to try different courses, and I got surprised by the content. Therefore is was very happy that I signed up for several courses and thereby could choose between those.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic level was amazing. I learned a lot while I was here.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is quite similar to UCPH, however the teaching style and the exams are different. I read less books and papers here but wrote more assignments and had to make more group work and presentations. In general I would say that I spend way more time on my studies here during the semester, but less time before the exams.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Usually the courses consist of lectures, excise classes, presentations and/or assignments. In most courses the assignments and presentations also count towards your final grad, why the exam only counts for maybe 50%.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Sustainable Investing (3 ECTS), Advanced Banking (6 ECTS), Experimental Economics (6 ECTS), Econometrics for Policy Analysts (6 ECTS), Global Switzerland (6 ECTS), Blockchain (3 ECTS).

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can really reccomend Econometrics for Policy Analysts if you want to learn how to interpret on economic analyses. It is a professor from Harvard (his name is David) that teaches in this course and he is really good. Also the Sustainable Investing course, here I learned a lot about ESG ratings. Be careful when you choose your courses. I chose Blockchain, which was a very interesting course, but it is only 3 ECTS and the workload was approximately the same as the 7.5 ECTS courses at UCPH.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: In the beginning there is a lot of administrative stuff that cost you a lot of money. For example when have to register at the Kreisbüro (corresponding to our kommunekontor) it costs 40-80 chf.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The transportation in Switzerland is very costfull. However the train system is super efficient. You can buy a half fare travel card for 120 chf (900 dkk) and thereby get discounts, which I will definitely reccomend. I also bought a monthly pass for zone 110 which cost 64 chf/month (450 dkk), and then if you want to travel you can buy day passes which is around 40-60 chf per day (250-500 dkk). Also meat is very expensive to buy. I will definitely reccomend you to eat lunch at the Mensa/cafeteria at UZH as it is cheap and good food, and cook dinner yourself in the evening.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very satisfied.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of welcome events where you can meet new students. Finance Club provide lunch every Thursday during the semester. Many parties and social activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The university provide the ASVZ app, which is the student sport association, Here you can enroll in different sports for free. I used it a lot to try out different sports.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel as much as you can in the beginning. Make sure to go on day trips to different parts of Switzerland before the exam period starts. In the winter season you can go skiing and in the summer season you can go hiking and camping in the mountains. The nature is amazing!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy as the culture is quite similar to the Danish culture. The Swiss people are quite reserved and are proud of their country. One of the things that I had to adjust to: the trains and trams are on time always. If you come 1 minute late you can be sure that it already left (and they excuse a lot for a couple of minutes delay).

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It can be hard to socialise with swiss students as they already have their friends. I recommend you to socialize with the exchange students and attend university events if you want to socialize with the swiss students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Some people cannot speak English (for example the employees in the Mensa/canteen at UZH), and unless you are really good at speaking German they can be really hard to understand. The swiss-german language is not the same as high-german as we learn in Denmark!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciate how polite and helpful the swiss people are. They are always ready to help you if you need anything. It is also very safe. I went home alone in the night several times, and it has never been an issue. We also went swimming in the lake several times leaving our phones/keys/etc. on the grass and nothing will ever happen.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. make sure to make enough money (in total I spent around 100,000 dkk), 2. reach out to new people (you need to be very openminded in the beginning, but it pays off afterwards), 3. remember to enjoy it, because time flies by so quickly!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I attended the German course in the first two weeks, which I will really recommend. It is a nice way to meet a lot of people, and to get to know the city before the semester starts.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I learned a lot about myself and my boundaries. I am better at speaking to new people without any prejudices, and I also learned when I want to be social and when I need some time alone.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The hygiene and the fact that I had to accept the risk of being sick.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
